text: Earth's mass is about 5.97 x 10^24 kg
as_written: about five point nine seven times ten to the twenty-fourth kilograms
source: NASA Goddard Planetary Fact Sheet (Earth)

text: Earth's mean density is about 5.5 g/cm3 (5,514 kg/m3)
as_written: average density is about five and a half grams per cubic centimetre
source: NASA Goddard Planetary Fact Sheet (Earth)

text: Gold's density is about 19.3 g/cm3
as_written: a density of about nineteen point three
source: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics

text: Gold is about 3.5 times as dense as Earth's average, so the same volume has about 3.5 times the mass
as_written: three and a half times as dense
source: Calculation: 19.3 / 5.51, using NASA Planetary Fact Sheet and CRC Handbook

text: A gold Earth of equal volume would have a mass of about 2 x 10^25 kg
as_written: about two times ten to the twenty-fifth kilograms
source: Calculation: 5.972e24 kg x 3.5

text: If mass were kept the same, a gold ball would be about two thirds as wide
as_written: only about two thirds as wide

text: Humans have mined a little over 200,000 tonnes of gold in total
as_written: a little over two hundred thousand tonnes
source: World Gold Council, Gold Supply and Demand statistics (above-ground stocks)

text: All mined gold would form a cube about 22 m on a side
as_written: a cube about twenty-two metres on each side
source: Calculation: about 216,000 t / 19,300 kg per m3, about 11,200 m3, cube root about 22 m

text: That volume equals roughly four and a half Olympic pools
as_written: roughly four and a half Olympic swimming pools
source: Calculation using the World Aquatics minimum pool volume of 2,500 m3

text: The planet of gold is about a hundred quadrillion times the volume of all mined gold
as_written: about a hundred quadrillion times larger than that cube
source: Calculation: Earth volume 1.08e21 m3 (NASA) / about 11,200 m3

text: World gold mine production is a bit over 3,000 tonnes a year
as_written: a bit over three thousand tonnes a year
source: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2025 (gold)

text: Neutron star merger GW170817 was detected on 17 August 2017, about 130 million light years away
as_written: the seventeenth of August, 2017, about one hundred and thirty million light years away
source: LIGO/Virgo collaboration, Abbott et al. 2017, Physical Review Letters 119, 161101

text: Models of the GW170817 kilonova suggest it forged from a few to over ten Earth masses of gold, with wide uncertainty
as_written: anywhere from a few to more than ten Earth masses of gold, with estimates varying
source: Kasen et al. 2017, Nature 551, 80; Pian et al. 2017, Nature 551, 67

text: A 2025 study proposed giant magnetar flares may supply roughly 1 to 10 percent of r-process elements
as_written: perhaps one to ten percent
source: Patel et al. 2025, Astrophysical Journal Letters (SGR 1806-20 giant flare)

text: Gold makes up roughly a billionth of the Sun's mass, so the Sun holds thousands of times less gold than the golden Earth
as_written: only about a billionth of the mass of the Sun
source: Asplund et al. 2009, Annual Review of Astronomy and Astrophysics 47, 481; solar mass from NASA Sun Fact Sheet

text: Surface gravity of a same-size gold Earth would be 3.5 times Earth's
as_written: three and a half times stronger
source: Calculation: g scales with mass at fixed radius

text: Earth's surface gravity is about 9.8 m/s2
as_written: about nine point eight metres per second squared
source: NASA Goddard Planetary Fact Sheet

text: Gravity on the gold Earth would be about 34 m/s2
as_written: about thirty-four
source: Calculation: 9.8 x 3.5

text: A 70 kg person would feel like about 245 kg
as_written: like two hundred and forty-five
source: Calculation: 70 x 3.5

text: Fighter pilots with g-suits tolerate up to about 9 g, briefly
as_written: up to about nine times normal gravity, but only for seconds
source: US Air Force / NASA aerospace physiology literature on sustained G tolerance

text: The Burj Khalifa is 828 m tall
as_written: eight hundred and twenty-eight metres
source: Council on Tall Buildings and Urban Habitat

text: Pressure at Earth's centre is about 360 GPa
as_written: about three hundred and sixty gigapascals
source: Dziewonski and Anderson 1981, Preliminary Reference Earth Model

text: 360 GPa is about 3.5 million times sea-level air pressure
as_written: three and a half million times the air pressure at sea level
source: Calculation: 360e9 Pa / 101,325 Pa

text: Central pressure scales with density squared, so more than ten times higher for gold at the same size
as_written: more than ten times higher
source: Calculation from hydrostatic scaling, P proportional to G rho^2 R^2: 3.5^2 = 12

text: Surface air pressure with the same atmosphere mass would be about 3.5 times higher
as_written: about three and a half times today's sea-level pressure
source: Calculation: pressure = column mass x g

text: 3.5 atmospheres corresponds to about 25 m of seawater depth
as_written: diving about twenty-five metres under the sea
source: Calculation: each 10 m of seawater adds about 1 atm; NOAA Diving Manual

text: Nitrogen narcosis begins at pressures near those of 3.5 atmospheres
as_written: it begins around the pressures you now live in
source: NOAA Diving Manual; US Navy Diving Manual
second_opinion_reason: The source and medical consensus state that nitrogen narcosis typically begins at partial pressures equivalent to 30 metres of depth (about 4 atmospheres), not 3.5 atmospheres.

text: Earth's atmospheric scale height is about 8.5 km
as_written: about eight and a half kilometres
source: NASA Goddard Earth Fact Sheet / standard atmosphere references

text: Scale height would be about 2.5 km at 3.5 g
as_written: about two and a half kilometres
source: Calculation: H = kT/mg, 8.5 / 3.5

text: Commercial jets cruise at about 11 km
as_written: a commercial jet cruising at eleven kilometres
source: FAA / typical cruise altitude, about 36,000 ft

text: The Moon's mean distance is about 384,400 km
as_written: about three hundred and eighty-four thousand kilometres
source: NASA Goddard Moon Fact Sheet

text: The Moon's mean orbital speed is about 1 km/s
as_written: about one kilometre per second
source: NASA Goddard Moon Fact Sheet (1.022 km/s)

text: With 3.5x Earth mass and unchanged Moon speed, perigee would be about 64,000 km
as_written: a little over sixty-four thousand kilometres
source: Calculation: Newtonian orbital mechanics, vis-viva and angular momentum conservation

text: The new orbital period would be about 6.5 days versus 27.3
as_written: about six and a half days instead of twenty-seven
source: Calculation: Kepler's third law; Moon sidereal period 27.3 d from NASA Moon Fact Sheet

text: The Roche limit for these densities is under 30,000 km
as_written: under thirty thousand kilometres
source: Calculation: fluid Roche limit 2.44 R (rho_planet/rho_moon)^(1/3)

text: Tidal force scales with the inverse cube of distance; six times closer gives 216 times
as_written: two hundred and sixteen times stronger
source: Calculation: 6^3 = 216

text: Present lunar equilibrium tide is about half a metre
as_written: half a metre or so
source: Standard tidal theory, equilibrium tide approximately 0.5 m; NOAA tides educational material

text: Everest is 8,849 m high
as_written: eight thousand eight hundred and forty-nine metres
source: Nepal and China joint survey, 2020

text: About 71 percent of Earth's surface is ocean
as_written: seventy-one percent
source: NOAA

text: The deepest ocean trench is nearly 11 km deep
as_written: nearly eleven kilometres down
source: NOAA / Challenger Deep surveys, about 10,900 m

text: JWST's mirror segments are gold coated, about 100 nm thick, 18 segments, about 48 grams of gold total
as_written: about one hundred nanometres thick, and the total gold on the whole mirror is only about forty-eight grams
source: NASA Webb Telescope mirror fact pages

text: Earth's total internal heat loss is about 47 terawatts
as_written: about forty-seven terawatts
source: Davies and Davies 2010, Solid Earth 1, 5

text: Roughly half of Earth's heat comes from radioactive decay, measured with geoneutrinos, with the split debated
as_written: roughly half of that is thought to come from radioactive decay
source: KamLAND and Borexino collaborations, geoneutrino measurements

text: Gold has one stable isotope, gold-197
as_written: only one stable isotope, gold one ninety-seven
source: IUPAC / Nubase atomic mass evaluation

text: Gold's thermal conductivity is about 318 W/m/K
as_written: about three hundred and eighteen watts per metre per kelvin
source: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics

text: Typical rock conductivity is about 2 to 3 W/m/K
as_written: two or three for typical rock
source: Clauser and Huenges 1995, Rock Physics and Phase Relations

text: Gold melts at 1,064 degrees Celsius at ordinary pressure
as_written: one thousand and sixty-four degrees Celsius
source: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics

text: Orbital speed at the surface would rise from 7.9 km/s to about 15 km/s; escape speed from 11.2 to about 21 km/s
as_written: about seven point nine kilometres per second to about fifteen, and the speed to escape from eleven point two to about twenty-one
source: Calculation: speeds scale with the square root of mass at fixed radius; baseline from NASA Planetary Fact Sheet

text: Super-Earths are planets of one to ten Earth masses and are common around other stars; the solar system has none
as_written: between one and ten Earth masses
source: NASA Exoplanet Archive / NASA Exoplanet Exploration

text: Earth's orbital period does not depend on the planet's mass; the year stays about 365 days
as_written: three hundred and sixty-five days
source: Kepler's third law; NASA Earth Fact Sheet

text: Post-tidal-circularisation Moon distance would be roughly 110,000 km
as_written: around a hundred and ten thousand kilometres
source: Calculation: angular momentum conservation, a(1-e^2) with perigee 64,000 km and apogee 384,400 km

text: Gold dissolves only in aqua regia or cyanide solutions, not in ordinary acids or water
as_written: you need a mixture called aqua regia, or something like cyanide
source: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics; standard inorganic chemistry

text: Chemical weathering and the carbon-silicate cycle regulate Earth's climate over geological time
as_written: carbon-silicate cycle
source: Walker, Hays and Kasting 1981, Journal of Geophysical Research 86, 9776
